questions.question: What is the difference between strong and durable? Give a processed material that has each property.
questions.expected_answer: Strong means a material can carry a heavy load or be pushed or pulled without breaking, like concrete or fired bricks. Durable means it lasts a long time without wearing out or rotting, like ceramic tiles, glass or fired bricks.

questions.question: Why should a home be built from fire-resistant and waterproof materials? Give examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Fire-resistant materials do not catch fire easily, so a house is less likely to burn down and fire is less likely to spread; examples are fired bricks, concrete, ceramic tiles, glass and metal. Waterproof materials keep rain and damp out; examples are glass, plastic pipes and sheets, glazed tiles, metal roof sheets and paint.

questions.question: Give one example each of a colourful and a textured material, and explain why the property is useful.
questions.expected_answer: Colourful: paint or dyed fabric like shweshwe, which makes things attractive and can send messages, like a red fire extinguisher. Textured: non-slip floor tiles or rubber shoe soles, which give grip so people do not slip, or a fluffy towel that soaks up water.
